notes.title: Brand New Multiplayer Modes and New Robot Pack DLCs Out Now!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27886209/2a2fd29273f5fc020e2cb78cb0dc4ca8dcf207e9.jpg[/img]

[h1]*** UP TO 70% DISCOUNT TO CELEBRATE NEW FEATURES ***[/h1]
[h1]ALL FOR ONE[/h1]
We've added another two new multiplayer modes to Insane Robots, bringing the total to six. All For One brings a single endurance battle mode to local and friends two-player battles. This really lets you build up your strategy, prepare your hand, and perhaps set up a surprise Special Boost move. But look out! Late game turns can create unexpected changes on everyone's robots. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27886209/483ae73a715a2f9c9016720d0f1e7cdda2689097.jpg[/img]

[h1]FAST 'N FURIOUS[/h1]
The second new mode is Fast 'n Furious, which brings three fast-paced cash battles to local and friends two-player battles. Turns are fast in this mode, as you only have 30s to act. Also life is low - all robots start with only 5 health. If you can keep up with the pace, you can make the moves to max the cash - go for overkill, damage, chains, and cash tokens to stay ahead of your opponent.

[h1]ROBOT PACKS 5 AND 6[/h1]
Unbelievably, we were so busy with the above, we forgot to let you know that we've also released two new Robot Pack DLCs. Each pack unlocks 4 robots, playable in local, friends and online multiplayer modes plus (NEW!) single-player quick battles. Every robot has 20 spoken insults you can throw at your opponents in the heat of battle!

[b]If you own Insane Robots Deluxe Edition or Season Pass, these packs will already be unlocked in your game.[/b]

Each pack is $2.99 on Steam, and gives you the following new robots:

[h1]Robot Pack 5[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27886209/6aeb72b1474a68123e81b32e79b544831edc84ea.png[/img]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/647170/Insane_Robots__Robot_Pack_5/
Promo: http://playni.ac/ir-promo-dlc5

* Scramble - Wakey waaakey…
* Darf Darf - Its bite is worse than its bark
* Ceph - Tentacled and highly advanced multi-tasker
* Unit 09785 - Waste disposal unit that thinks you are trash

[h1]Robot Pack 6
[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27886209/ee8d4d443086ca9d00d71e19111a72059ee18763.png[/img]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/647171/Insane_Robots__Robot_Pack_6/
Promo: http://playni.ac/ir-promo-dlc6

* Cutlaz - Arisen from the black seas of infinity
* Kröm - Assassin. Hitbot. Contract scrapper.
* Icebox - Rogue cryo-science bot
* Cypod - It's got its eye on you

[h1]OTHER STUFF[/h1]
There are also some tweaks and fixes in this build. Normal and Tricksy modes now both unlock tokens a bit faster, and AI robots cannot now unlock the Cloud and Clear achievement for you - oops!

notes.title: One month on: review roundup, accolades, and things we're fixing!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/27886209/a945b4af3c1336126efcfbd1db141e270063a341.png[/img]

With Insane Robots out for almost a month, we thought we'd round up some of the fantastic reviews we've had. There have been a load of 8/10, 910 and even 10/10 scores and reviewers have said some lovely things. 

Here are the links for the reviews above, plus a few more we couldn't fit in!

"One of the best indie titles of this generation” - 10/10 - Windows Central
http://playni.ac/ir-article-windowscentral

“One of the closest things to perfect I've seen in quite some time” - 8/10 - Shack News
http://playni.ac/ir-article-shacknews2

“One of the most original card battle games in recent history” - 8/10 - FNGR GNS
http://playni.ac/ir-article-fngrgns

“Get right down to throwing rectangles at each other like the robot god intended” - PC Gamer
http://playni.ac/ir-article-pcgamer

“I’m massively impressed by the balance here” - Rock, Paper, Shotgun
http://playni.ac/ir-article-rps

“Vibrant and energetic." - 9/10 - Xbox Tavern
http://playni.ac/ir-article-xboxtavern

“A very fun pick-up-and-play title” - 8/10 - Gamereactor
http://playni.ac/ir-article-gamereactor

“Absolutely smashes the gameplay” - 8/10 - Gert Lush Gaming
http://playni.ac/ir-article-gert

“Tremendous fun.” - 8/10 - The Xbox Hub
http://playni.ac/ir-article-xboxhub2

“An insanely good game” - 8/10 - Blast Away
http://playni.ac/ir-article-blastaway

“A card game unlike any other” - 8/10 - Absolute Xbox
http://playni.ac/ir-article-absolutexbox

“Highly recommended.” - 8/10 - XBLA Fans
http://playni.ac/ir-article-xblafans

“A rare joy” - 8/10 - SquareXO
http://playni.ac/ir-article-squarexo

“A great experience, one you’d be insane to pass by.” - 9/10 - Xbox Addict
http://playni.ac/ir-article-xboxaddict

“Completely delicious.” - 8/10 - Canard PC
http://playni.ac/ir-article-canard

"Hits a sweet spot." - 8/10 - True Achievements
http://playni.ac/ir-article-trueachievements

Finally, we're aware of a couple of issues that reviewers (and you) have mentioned:

1) Loading time

Good news! We already addressed this in free update V1.0.6 and there is now a "fast loading" option in the settings menu that makes transitions between sections of the game go like lightning, giving you barely enough time to read the help tips.

2) Online 2P matchmaking wait time

I'm afraid there's not a lot we can do to address this until there are a lot more people playing online. With a 1v1 game, we would require players arriving in the lobby on average every 2 minutes to give only a 2 minute waiting time, however that would mean over 720 people a day trying to play. This is only a rough calculation, but you get the idea.

We have added a notification sound (an exhultation from the Spark) when an online 2P battle initiates, which will help if you are not looking at your screen.

The good news is, (1) you can play local 2-player, (2) you can play against Steam friends, and, finally, (3) we are hosting a series of multiplayer sessions every Thurs where you can play against the community and the developers! To find out more, look on Steam, Twitter (http://playni.ac/ir-twitter), and our Discord server (http://playni.ac/discord).

notes.title: Insane Robots V1.0.6 Update: Volume Controls and Fast Loading!
notes.content:
We've been listening to some of your feedback in the Steam forums and on our Discord (http://playni.ac/discord). We've been hard at work today to bring some much requested features (and a couple of fixes) to Insane Robots for a first day update. So here goes!

We've:

* added volume controls! Just simple volume setting for music and sound effects in both options and pause menus.
* added a “fast load” mode, that fast skips loading screens if you don’t want to read the help info there; there's a new toggle button on the options and pause menus. The game will also automatically switch to fast load mode after a while (but this can be disabled in options).
* added arrows to tournament complete and quick battle complete panels to subtly signal how stars are earned.
* fixed the leaderboard paging and number of entries.
* stopped 0 scores being entered in the leaderboard
* corrected text errors in 2 stories.

Insane Robots V1.0.6 is out now. Enjoy the day one update!

notes.title: Conquer a robot dystopia in cute card battler Insane Robots
notes.content:
Playniac insists Insane Robots is not a card game. It's a card battler, meaning its cards are just weapons and strategic tools, not items to be collected. It doesn't have "costly expansions or time-consuming customization," the studio says. You pick a robot, build a deck that matches their abilities, and get right down to throwing rectangles at each other like the robot god intended. Not only that, it evolved from a prototype of a board game, so genetically it's probably closer to a deck builder like Dominion than a CCG like Hearthstone. 

Insane Robots features multiplayer battles and leaderboards, but it also sports a full-fat single-player campaign. You play as a robot vigilante leading a rebellion in a dystopian machine society. You can choose from 46 playable robots, whose play styles can be further customized with over 100 abilities called augments. No matter who you choose, you'll be fighting countless enemy robots in randomly generated arenas, upgrading your deck as you progress. Playniac says the flow of Insane Robot's campaign will feel familiar to fans of roguelikes, especially FTL. (It's also quite similar to Slay the Spire which, funnily enough, just added its third playable character: a robot.) 

If the card battles are the meat of the game, then the arenas are the potatoes. They play out as grid-based mini-strategy games with environmental hazards and branching story events. In other words, the decisions you make in arenas will affect your standing in battles, so you're not just moving around. 

Insane Robots is scheduled to release on July 12.
